title.narrative: Fostering innovative start-ups in Kenya, Rwanda, and Tanzania

description.narrative: The history of ‘Urbanization’ is the history of ‘Industrialization’. The growing number of people migrating to emerging industrial cities from the municipal communities led to the high population density causing various problems that cities are facing now such as shortage of adequate housing, basic services, urban infrastructures, and devastating impacts of climate change. Under this rapid urbanization, ‘Start-ups’ can be flexible engines and catalysts that provide creative and innovative solutions to tackle the urban challenges and achieve urban economic growth. In particular, expectations remain high for start-ups in LDC (Less Developed Countries) suffering from detrimental impacts caused by rapid urbanisation. UN-HABITAT is also paying attention to the methodologies for incubating and empowering potential of local start-ups, equipping them with creative ideas, advanced technologies by which to fuel urban economic sustainability. Against this backdrop, in June 2019, UN-Habitat and Korean SMEs and Startups Agency (KOSME) signed a Letter of Intent agreed to collaborate in the “Korea-Africa programme for fostering start-ups enterprises and experience sharing through cooperation between start-ups”. This cooperation has paid attention to African continent, where small and medium start-ups account for more than half of GDP and employment in most countries, having vast potential to drive long-term economic growth and social transformation in Africa. Start-ups not only provide decent job opportunities to local youth but also innovative solutions to resolve unbalanced growth and absolute poverty in African countries to create a better urban future. To take follow-up measures, KOSME with the Korean National Committee for UN-Habitat (KNCUH) jointly organized ‘Korea-Kenya Innovative Start-up Conference and Business Meeting’ in 2020 and ‘Korea-Kenya Online Training Program on Start-up Policies’, ‘Korea-Uganda Innovative Start-up Conference and Business Meeting’ in 2021. Due to the Covid-19 pandemic over the last two years, the programs took place online, thus more substantive construction of global partnerships and networking remained to be improved. Nevertheless, the participants evaluated the programs informative and educative, and expected more engagements and exchanges with Korean start-up entrepreneurs, policymakers, and potential investors.
